events.title: Americans open to data centers with guardrails, poll finds
events.summary: AI companies can soften support for statewide data center moratoriums like New York’s by committing to pay for related electricity costs and lessen local environmental impacts, according to a new poll from major firms in both parties. The research was conducted by Fabrizio Ward and Impact Research — run by Trump pollster Tony Fabrizio and Biden pollster John Anzalone, respectively — on behalf of the American Infrastructure Alliance, a coalition of AI companies, private equity firms, and labor unions advocating for “responsible” data center development. Fifty-eight percent of those polled nationwide said they oppose building data centers in their state, according to results shared first with Semafor. But 54% said they would actually support data center construction if companies pledged to cover electricity costs, protect consumers from higher utility bills, and safeguard surrounding environmental resources; 31% still opposed data center construction outright. The poll also found that seven in 10 voters worry that outright moratoriums on AI data centers could lead to China having more control over infrastructure that houses US information. Meanwhile, 64% said they’re concerned that bans will lead to jobs, investment, and economic growth going to other states instead.

Open-weight models can be significantly more cost-efficient and can also offer transparency and flexibility that closed source models don’t allow. events.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps
events.summary: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI. Alongside the launch of the company’s new AI wearables from Bee , Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk more in depth about where he sees personal computing headed. “A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.” By “ambient devices,” he means those that work quietly in the background, using sensors and AI to help you figure out what needs to be done, instead of the other way around, where you’re telling the device what you need to do. “As it works in the background, you’re able to stay more present. You’re able to get more done. You’re about to spend more time with people … you’re not afraid if you miss something. It’s incredibly powerful,” Panay said. Amazon’s biggest entry into this space is the set of new Bee devices it introduced on Thursday, which include a band you can wear on your wrist or detach to wear as a pendant, as well as a new credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of your smartphone. These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to. To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done. Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls. That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them. Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work. “You have to give customers that control,” he said. “Every product is different, but for Bee specifically, as an example in the ambient space like that, you have to design with privacy in mind. And that’s what we do. That’s critical.” The executive, who came to Amazon after 19 years at Microsoft where he oversaw the development of Surface devices, has spent a lot of his life thinking about how personal computing will evolve. With Bee — and ambient computing more generally — Panay also envisioned a future where the idea of interacting with apps becomes less important, as more tasks are handled via AI. “Do I think we have a future where there’s a bit of a balance — a whole generation that doesn’t say ‘give me the app’ for that, but says it should just understand what I need? Yeah, I do. I think that transformation is coming. I think that is the next generation,” he said. That doesn’t necessarily mean the smartphone itself won’t continue to be an important personal computing device (as much as Amazon would like it to be an Alexa tablet or Echo smart speaker), Panay pointed out. Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you. “I’m not a proponent that says one form factor is going to replace another. I don’t think that’s the case,” he clarified. “I think there’s an intelligence layer that connects it all … and it has to be useful.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . events.title: Trump administration advances plan for peptide drugs favored by RFK Jr.
events.summary: Federal health officials are moving ahead with plans to broaden access to a class of unproven injectable drugs called peptides WASHINGTON -- U.S. health officials are moving ahead with a plan to allow specialty pharmacies to produce certain peptides , a class of largely unregulated injections that have become popular among followers of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and other wellness influencers. Kennedy's Department of Health and Human Services submitted a peptides “interim access policy” to the White House for review, according to a posting Thursday on a government website. The plan was sent to the Office of Management and Budget, which reviews federal rules and regulations with the potential for significant economic impact. HHS officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Thursday afternoon. Peptides are the building blocks of more complex proteins, triggering hormones inside the body needed for growth, metabolism and healing. Drug companies have brought several to market as medications, including mainstay treatments for diabetes and weight loss . But the ones at issue here haven’t gone through that rigorous vetting process. Nevertheless, they have gained a foothold among Americans interested in bulking up, looking younger or boosting energy. Those uses are not approved by the Food and Drug Administration and most of the data on peptides comes from animal studies. Before joining the administration, Kennedy publicly declared that “FDA’s war” on peptides and other wellness products would soon end. After becoming health secretary, Kennedy said U.S. compounding pharmacies must be allowed to sell peptides because Americans were increasingly turning to “gray market” peptides made in China and other countries. Those products remain widely available for purchase via online platforms like TikTok. The White House filing doesn’t give specifics of the new policy, but two people familiar with the plan say it is intended to allow pharmacies to temporarily compound some of the most popular peptides, including BPC-157, a chemical promoted to build muscle and heal injuries. The people spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential government deliberations. The update is the latest indication that Kennedy and other Trump administration officials are looking to ease access to unproven products that are popular within the Make America Healthy Again movement. Some of the biggest MAHA figures sell peptide injections and supplements. The FDA previously placed BPC-157 and more than a dozen other injectable peptides on its list of substances that are too risky to be compounded by pharmacies. Possible risks include contamination, allergic reactions and tumor growth, according to the FDA. But earlier this year, Kennedy directed the agency to reconsider a short list of chemicals that have been widely promoted by wellness influencers and fitness celebrities. Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say Fort Hood survivors speak out on Pentagon's decision to livestream Hasan's execution Hurricane Isaias: At least 4 dead as Isaias downgraded In July, a panel of external FDA advisers recommended the agency drop its restrictions on six of the seven peptides put before them. That recommendation went against the scientific conclusion of FDA’s staff scientists, who reiterated that none of the peptides had been studied enough to establish their safety and effectiveness. The new policy sent to the White House would essentially assure compounding pharmacies — specialty businesses that mix customized medications that aren’t available from traditional drugmakers — that they won't be targeted for producing certain peptides, according to the people familiar with the plan. That approach, known as enforcement discretion, allows the FDA to selectively choose to not enforce some of its own regulations. Formally adding the peptides to FDA's list of drugs that are safe for compounding would require federal rulemaking, a process that could take years and involves multiple rounds of public comment. It was not immediately clear if the administration still plans to pursue that process. The proposal was quickly praised online by some Kennedy allies who sell peptides. “This is huge,” Brigham Buhler, a wellness clinic operator who sells peptides through an online service, posted on X. “This isn’t about whether you’re for or against peptides. It’s about whether you’re for or against MEDICAL FREEDOM.” The panel of outside experts that met in July was selected by Kennedy's health department and included several doctors, pharmacists and consultants who work in the peptide field. The peptide business has caught the attention of major telehealth providers, including Hims & Hers and Noom. Both companies recently announced plans to offer peptides to their customers if the federal government eases access. Wall Street analysts estimate the market could be worth $2 billion to $3 billion.

events.title: Bluesky wants to make it easier to buy, sell, and fundraise on the network
events.summary: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Bluesky plans to introduce payments in the coming months, a first step in its strategy to make money without relying on advertising. CEO Toni Schneider and COO Rose Wang outlined the plans Thursday at TechCrunch Disrupt , explaining how the company hopes to build on the commerce and fundraising activity already happening on its decentralized social network. “People are actually selling things, fundraising very successfully, supporting each other on the network,” Schneider said. “We want to make that easier, and the way we’re going to do this is if you see something on the network that you like and support, you can support that monetarily, and we want to do it in a way that works for Bluesky and for all the other apps out there as well, so that it works across the entire network.” Schneider, the former CEO of Automattic, took the reins of the company in March after longtime CEO Jay Graber stepped down. He said, while onstage, that he was surprised by the reaction to his appointment, with some users joking that it marked the beginning of the end for the platform. Those comments reflected fears that a leadership change would bring unwanted changes to Bluesky. Schneider said he understands that users can leave Bluesky for another platform if the company introduces features or changes they dislike, a reality that he said keeps the leadership team accountable as it prepares to introduce monetization in the coming months. The executives argued that advertising isn’t the only viable business model for a social network. “I think there’s a story around monetization that feels like advertising is the inevitable thing we have to do that will ruin the network,” Wang said. “What was really promising about having Toni join us is he built at WordPress Automatic a $10 billion business where a billion of it goes back to the parent company and the rest of it goes to the ecosystem.” Wang also pointed to Bluesky’s status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), which she said puts the company’s mission at the center of its business strategy. “Yes, we need to make money, but because of our infrastructure, we cannot lock people in,” Wang said. “And so the thing that really matters for us is the people who are creating value on the networks these days are the ones who are getting the value that is coming in or the money that’s coming in. And I kind of think of it as like feudal society where we’re working for a few landlords and they dictate everything, and then we have to pay up our dues as tariffs.” Bluesky aims to give users ownership of their digital identities and control over their networks while creating a more open internet where value and revenue can flow directly to the people who generate them. “First, we’ll start with payments, but I think it’s about disrupting the actual infrastructure layer, which is what we’re doing, and not just building another app,” Wang said. events.title: US imposes Iran-related sanctions on Iraq Development Bank
events.summary: The Iraq Development Bank, among dozens of other targets, was hit with sanctions by the US on Thursday for its relations with Iran , the Treasury Department said in a statement. The bank was one of 10 entities and 16 people hit in the latest round of sanctions under Washington's “Economic Outcast” programme. US President Donald Trump's administration has warned countries and companies that continue to do business with Iran would face significant consequences. “Working with partners across the US government, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds,” the department said. The Treasury has previously imposed sanctions on banks in Turkey and a Bank Melli branch in the UAE, among others. The UAE Central Bank last month banned Bank Melli Iran from conducting transactions between its branches in the UAE and Iran after an investigation. Mr Trump's administration has hoped its “Economic Outcast” programme would sever Iran's remaining economic lifelines and force the regime to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. “The noose is tightening around Iran’s economy, and not even Iran’s so-called allies can save it,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said. Iraq in 2024 banned the IDB and seven other local commercial banks from engaging in US dollar transactions. The Treasury said the IDB has abused the now-dissolved dollar wire auction and maintains ties to Iran government entities and militia groups in Iraq. It is one of dozens of Iraqi banks that have been cut off for years due to concerns over sanctions evasion, money laundering and illicit finance. The US holds significant influence over Baghdad's financial policies because its international oil revenue is held at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi has sought to work with US authorities on the country's banking sector , which for years has been marred by corruption. Hiba Abdulwahib, an Iraqi researcher and analyst, said Thursday's move should not be viewed as a punishment for Iraq and it does not necessarily indicate that the US believes Mr Al Zaidi's government is unwilling to reform its banking sector. "Authority in Iraq is fragmented," she said. "The government does not have effective control over every institution or economic actor operating inside the country. I believe Washington understands those limitations, especially when it comes to Iran’s networks in Iraq." Ms Abdulwahib also said she expected the pressure of sanctions to lead to more co-ordination on closer oversight, monitoring of suspicious activities and penalties for breaches. "Baghdad has an incentive to address these problems before Washington imposes further sanctions, and the banks themselves have to take that risk seriously," she said. In July, the Treasury's Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence outlined a years-long plan that would eventually allow restricted Iraq banks to be reintegrated into the US dollar system. The process would include an initial phase of reforms from the Central Bank of Iraq, with the second phase consisting of a restricted bank completing the entire reform and licensing process. This would involve successfully undertaking a third-party audit of their compliance function, securing a qualified investor and meeting international standards. The department at the time said “no banned banks have regained access to foreign currency transactions”. "The United States will not tolerate the abuse of Iraqi banks by Iran-aligned militia groups and will take independent action, if necessary, to target such activity,” it said. The move coincided with Mr Al Zaidi's visit to the US, where he had pledged to disarm militia groups in the country by September 30. In an interview with The New York Times in September, Mr Al Zaidi pushed that timeline to June 2027. The disarmament is a crucial part of how he is expected to manage Iraq's relations with the US and Iran.

events.title: New Medicare season begins, but some shifts will arrive in 2027
events.summary: Open enrollment for Medicare plans begins Thursday, allowing people to choose between traditional Medicare and Medicare Advantage plans until Dec. 7 WASHINGTON -- Open enrollment for Medicare plans begins Thursday and enrollees will face a slew of changes that go into effect in 2027. During the enrollment period, which ends Dec. 7, people will have the opportunity to choose between traditional Medicare and privately run Medicare Advantage plans in their area, as well as prescription drug plans. Those changes go into effect on Jan. 1. Open enrollment also comes as inflation adds pressure on seniors whose healthcare costs have risen and as midterm elections are weeks away. Voters have consistently said that the cost of living is a major concern heading into the elections. The Medicare enrollment period also comes as the Social Security Administration announced Wednesday that the annual cost-of-living adjustment for older adults and people with disabilities will go up by 3.6% beginning in 2027, which translates to $75 extra per month for the nearly 72 million people who receive monthly Social Security benefits and about 7.3 million beneficiaries who get Supplemental Security Income. New changes to Medicare coming in 2027 include higher Part D out-of-pocket caps, the end of temporary federal Part D premium subsidies, and new drug price negotiations. Juliette Cubanski, director of KFF’s program on Medicare policy, said the open enrollment period offers enrollees “an opportunity to evaluate the coverage they have and see if there might be better options for them in terms of accessing the care that they need at possibly a lower cost.” Here are a few of the biggest changes: The cap on annual out-of-pocket expenses for Medicare Part D drugs will increase to $2,400, up from $2,100 in 2026, and the standard deductible will increase from $615 to $700. The temporary Part D premium subsidy will also end early. The Trump administration concludes at year’s end a temporary Medicare Part D subsidy program that has helped offset premiums. It was initially implemented by former President Joe Biden's administration in 2024 to lower patients’ Medicare Part D prescription drug costs in response to the effects of the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has projected only modest price increases for most people. CMS did not respond to an Associated Press request for comment. David Lipschutz, co-director of the Center for Medicare Advocacy, points out that there could be greater disruptions in coverage for some Medicare enrollees since some Medicare Advantage plans are pulling out of specific geographic areas and scaling back benefits, such as dental coverage, while potentially increasing cost-sharing. Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say Fort Hood survivors speak out on Pentagon's decision to livestream Hasan's execution Hurricane Isaias: At least 4 dead as Isaias downgraded Plans, insurance companies make business decisions about what they’re going to offer the following year, if they’re going to offer anything at all. And by that very nature, it causes disruption to the system. And it looks like this time there’s more disruption than usual. New Medicare-negotiated prices, part of a Biden-era law that allows the haggling for Medicare, will go into effect for 15 drugs, including weight-loss and diabetes medications Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy. Additionally, Trelegy Ellipta, Xtandi, Pomalyst, Ibrance, Ofev, Linzess, Calquence, Austedo/Austedo XR, Breo Ellipta, Tradjenta, Xifaxan, Vraylar, Janumet/Janumet XR, and Otezla will be covered by Medicare as of Jan. 1. CMS expects the change to lower prescription drug coverage for people enrolled in Medicare by $685 million in 2027. AARP’s Executive Vice President and Chief Advocacy Officer Nancy LeaMond said in a statement that “higher healthcare costs are making it harder for older Americans to afford the care they need." “It’s more important than ever to shop around, compare your options, and choose the coverage that’s best for you," she said. Along with the changes, President Donald Trump in recent weeks made a series of promises to Medicare enrollees and retirees. Last week, Trump said his administration will make one-time payments of $90 per person in October to help more than 20 million Medicare enrollees — or less than one third of enrollees — pay for their Part B premiums. It will cost about $2 billion. Not eligible are roughly 35 million Medicare Advantage enrollees, millions of other people with disabilities and low-income Medicare recipients. According to the CMS website, eligible beneficiaries will receive one $90 rebate this month, with most getting a direct deposit. Others will receive a paper check from the Treasury Department later in October. Trump also announced recently that roughly 1 million people would get rebate checks of $500 for Affordable Care Act premiums.

events.title: ‘Close to zero’: AI chiefs reckon with ‘politics projects’ and the level of true change in response to AI
events.summary: Few large organizations have rebuilt their core operations around artificial intelligence, according to the technology chief of one of the world’s largest consulting firms. He also said companies shouldn’t yet spend much energy on assigning blame when AI projects go wrong. The number of large enterprises or government processes “that have been really, truly reinvented with AI at the absolute core is basically close to zero,” Marc Warner, Accenture’s global chief technology officer, said during a Fortune Brainstorm AI virtual event. Accenture is a founding partner of Brainstorm AI and sponsored the event. Warner and three other executives spoke with Fortune AI editor Jeremy Kahn about why many companies report little return from AI despite wide use. The other panelists were Matthieu Caillat of AXA , Greg Ulrich of Mastercard , and Marjorie Janiewicz of Mistral AI. Their answers pointed less to software than to organizational change. Edges versus core Warner said most companies have put AI in peripheral work such as marketing, meeting notes, and transcription. Coding is “perhaps a little different,” because returns there can be measured. Changing the economics of an industry, he said, means targeting core business processes, which is risky. He compared the moment to early factories that used electricity only for lighting, before redesigning production around electric motors. Ulrich said the biggest returns come from redesigning whole workflows, not layering AI onto existing ones. He said Mastercard is “very, very advanced” in redesigning its product development life cycle, with smaller teams and faster turnaround. He also described a trap: speed up one step in an 80-step process and the next step simply develops a backlog. “The AI agent to automate a piece of this isn’t … the long pole in the tent for a lot of this,” Ulrich said. “It’s the rethinking. It’s the remapping.” Warner called AI transformations “politics projects” and said he had thought of them as technology projects until recently. He said he still sees the AI builds themselves as technology projects. Caillat said that as technology improves, the work is less about technology and more about, “How do you bring people along?” Ulrich said Mastercard relies on CEO sponsorship, including weekly updates with the CEO’s direct reports, but added that no one has solved the politics of large organizations. Accountability Kahn asked an audience question about who is responsible when an AI agent goes wrong. Warner said there is no single clean answer. In general, he said, the business owner is accountable for an agent’s value, the technologist for its functionality, and the chief information security officer for its security. He then said most companies shouldn’t dwell on fault yet. “I don’t think most organizations should be worrying too much about the blame game right now,” Warner said, urging companies to give people credit for trying things, knowing many will fail. He made an exception for critical incidents such as a major security breach. Janiewicz, who said she spent 10 years in cybersecurity, agreed that finger-pointing isn’t useful. She said the better question is whether a company controls the technology it adopts and can set its own guardrails. Mistral sells open-weight models that customers can run on their own infrastructure. Keeping pace Executives also said their plans have a short shelf life. Ulrich said consulting tools Mastercard built about a year ago are now “quaint, and just not that useful today,” so the company is rebuilding them. Caillat said AXA used to “measure twice and cut once” and “can’t afford that anymore,” because conclusions expire before certainty arrives. Caillat said AXA started with about 400 AI use cases to build enthusiasm, then narrowed its focus. He said the insurer’s plan for 2027 to 2029 targets €500 million to €700 million a year in recurring pretax value from AI by 2029, and that AXA has about 4 billion unstructured documents it is starting to use. Warner said that, by Accenture’s calculations, the pace shows no sign of slowing until something approaching 2030. Energy constraints in the West could start to bite in the early 2030s, he said. Accenture is the founding partner of Fortune Brainstorm AI events and hosted this session. Generative AI was used for research assistance and/or transcription for this article. The reporter independently reported and verified the factual claims in this article, and a human editor reviewed it before publication. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: The AI era will redefine business
events.summary: Reed’s view One of the most profound takeaways from my interview with Reflection AI co-founder and CTO Ioannis Antonoglou this week on Semafor’s Future Proof is his declaration that the AI era will force us to redefine what each business actually does and rebuild it from the ground up, using AI as scaffolding. And that is going to take decades, a lot longer than most people in Silicon Valley project. Right now, we are thinking about data all wrong. Today, businesses mostly capture data that’s measurable or the result of some kind of work product. What’s usually not captured is the work itself — the difficult-to-define causal link that connects all of the actions that a company takes. “A lot of the context is like, ‘we jump on a call, or someone shared something or said something’” Antonoglou told me. I’ve been thinking about that challenge with my own work. How can a journalist capture gut feelings about what might make a good story? (It’s a bit like that famous 1960s US Supreme Court case on pornography, “you know it when you see it.“) What about capturing how reporters decide who to call first, or what questions to ask to get the most revealing answers? In the AI era, Antonoglou told me, companies have to throw out what they’ve done for decades and come up with new ways to measure and carry out their work. That’s part of what Antonoglou is trying to help customers do with his company’s open-weight models. “It will take maybe a decade or two decades before people really rethink how things are done and how they can just do them with AI in mind,” he said. It won’t happen in every industry at the same time — probably a good thing for the economy’s stability — but it does provide another new entry for startups that move faster than incumbents to spring ahead. Notable Nvidia is in early talks to acquire Reflection AI , Financial Times reported.

events.title: US consumers are muscling through higher prices, but for how long?
events.summary: High gas prices are intensifying inflation and vacuuming up more of Americans’ dollars, yet consumers are still digging deep to spend, powering the economy, at least for now WASHINGTON -- WASHINGTON (AP) — High gas prices are intensifying inflation and vacuuming up more of Americans' dollars, yet consumers are still digging deep to spend , powering the economy, at least for now . A slew of economic data Thursday showed that inflation accelerated last month as more expensive oil and gas began to lift prices in other parts of the economy, including shipping and warehousing, before the increases reach most Americans. Wholesale food prices jumped, which could make groceries more expensive in the months ahead. At the same time, consumers also ramped up their spending, according to data released Thursday. Though much of the increase reflected higher prices, consumer resilience is powering solid U.S. economic growth. Workers are enjoying an unusual degree of job security despite scattered layoffs, which likely encourages spending despite surveys showing that many Americans have a gloomy economic outlook. It all adds up to an economy in which people are spending money but don't feel good about it. “Consumers may have gritted their teeth and looked through higher gas prices,” said Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisers. “They're not happy, but they're still spending.” A report Thursday on wholesale prices helps explain the gloom: The government's producer price index, which measures costs before they reach the consumer, jumped 6.3% in September from a year earlier, the biggest increase in nearly four years . On a monthly basis, prices soared 1.3% from August to September, powered by a 20% rise in gas prices. Higher diesel prices have made shipping more expensive because long-haul trucks and freight trains rely on the fuel. Higher transportation costs may have helped push up food costs, which rose 1.2% from August to September, the biggest monthly gain since February. The wholesale price report followed the latest consumer price figures, released Wednesday, which showed inflation rising to 3.7% in September, far above the Federal Reserve's 2% target. “The jolt to transportation prices affects every good in the economy, since inputs to manufacturing move to factories and goods at all stages of production move from producer to wholesaler to retailer by truck, train or rail,” wrote Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics. “This is how increases in energy prices ‘bleed through’ to prices of core goods.” Farmers also rely on diesel to power most of their equipment, which could further push up food prices. Diesel prices averaged $6.32 a gallon nationwide Thursday, according to AAA, up from just $3.66 a year ago. Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say Fort Hood survivors speak out on Pentagon's decision to livestream Hasan's execution Atlanta school worker dies after falling from Six Flags roller coaster in Georgia Despite those cost pressures, retail sales rose a solid 0.8% from August, more than economists had forecast. The increase was driven by a 6.4% jump in spending at gas stations, but consumers also spent elsewhere, including a healthy 1.1% rise at restaurants and bars. Economists say that as long as unemployment stays low and Americans continue working, spending will likely stay resilient. Hiring has been sluggish, but layoffs are also unusually low. Another report Thursday showed that the number of people seeking unemployment benefits stayed below 200,000 last week, a historically low figure. Applications for unemployment aid are a proxy for layoffs. “If the unemployment rate remains low, meaning consumers have a job, they will continue to spend, even if more cautiously and leaning increasingly on savings and credit,” Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, said in an email. Many economists worry, however, that as inflation stays high, it will steadily erode Americans' spending power and start to weigh on the economy. Weekly paychecks, adjusted for inflation, actually declined in September compared with a year ago for the first time since May. And September hiring slowed to a disappointing 29,000 jobs from a revised 133,000 in August, according to the Labor Department early this month. The unemployment rate ticked higher to 4.2% from the previous month, which is still low. Yet economists had expected September payrolls to come in around 90,000. Stubbornly elevated inflation also means the Federal Reserve will likely raise its key interest rate in the coming months in an effort to slow spending and bring down inflation. When the Fed raises its rate, that can raise borrowing costs for mortgages, car loans, and credit cards over time. According to minutes released from the most recent meeting, most Fed officials expect that another interest rate increase will likely be needed this year to combat inflation.

events.title: US retail trade group forecasts healthy holiday sales, in part due to inflation
events.summary: Don’t underestimate U.S. shoppers when it comes to shelling out money for the winter holidays NEW YORK -- Don't count out U.S. shoppers when it comes to shelling out money for the winter holidays despite higher fuel prices and other financial pressures. The nation's largest retail trade group said Thursday that it expects American consumers will collectively spend $1.01 trillion this November and December, which would be 4.2% more than during the same months last year. The increase reflects more than seasonal good cheer, according to economists. The National Retail Federation and other organizations that have issued holiday forecasts said they expected higher consumer prices to account for about half of the anticipated growth. Moreover, higher income shoppers will fuel a lot of the spending, retail experts say. “We all acknowledge households continue to navigate persistent inflation and uneven confidence about the economy,” National Retail Federation President and CEO Matthew Shay told reporters on Thursday. “But throughout the year, consumers have repeatedly shown that holidays and spending on loved ones are priorities. We’re confident that pattern is going to continue through the 2026 winter holidays.” Retailers rang up $972 billion in holiday sales last year, which was 3.1% more than the year before that, the trade group said. At 4.2%, NRF's growth projection is above the actual gains from the last 20 years, which averaged 3.1% when excluding the outsized holiday spending of pandemic-era 2020 and 2021, according to Mark Mathews, the trade group's chief economist. The forecast, which was not adjusted for inflation, is in line with most other holiday predictions so far. The outlooks illustrate an ongoing disconnect between the dismal consumer confidence that shows up in monthly surveys and Americans' willingness to keep spending. The U.S. war with Iran has driven up gasoline prices for drivers and caused worries about all kinds of products getting more expensive as high diesel prices make transporting goods costlier for retailers. The average price for regular gasoline rose to $4.33 per gallon Thursday, according to motor club AAA. Before the war began, gas cost less than $3 a gallon. Experts say such higher pump prices will continue to squeeze lower-income shoppers, while higher-income shoppers buoyed by stock market gains will keep splurging on discretionary purchases. “We’ve seen disruption after disruption kind of knock people off kilter, and then the consumer comes roaring back,” Bryan Eshelman, a partner and managing director at AlixPartners, said. Instead of pulling back altogether, consumers are changing their shopping habits by trading down to lower-price brands and stores, shopping earlier and relying more on credit cards and buy now pay later plans , Eshelman said. Average long-term US mortgage rate holds at 7.4%, remaining at highest level in nearly 3 years Roof collapse at Pakistan school kills 33 Some grocery prices are soaring, while others are plunging. Here's what to know Holiday spending accounts for 19% of the U.S. retail industry's annual sales, even more for some types of retailers, according to NRF. Economists look at the holiday results as a gauge for the state of the consumer beyond the holidays. Consumer spending is monitored closely because it drives about 70% of U.S. gross domestic product. “It not only tells us about the current state of the consumer, (but) it helps inform expectations for the year ahead as well," Mastercard Economics Institute chief economist Michelle Meyer said. “It gives us a lot of incredible insights into how consumers are doing from a macro perspective.” The institute, which tracks spending across all payment methods including cash, forecast a 5.5% increase in holiday sales from Nov. 1 through Dec. 24 compared to last year. Although Mastercard estimated that half of the growth would come from higher prices instead of more sales, the institute still expects healthy spending by shoppers because of a decent U.S. job market, Meyer said. “I guess they feel some sense of security because the jobless numbers are so low," she said. AlixPartners expects holiday sales numbers for October, November and December to expand 4% to 7% over the same three months last year, the firm said. Adobe expects U.S. online sales to hit $275 billion this holiday season, representing 6.7% growth. That growth is a tad smaller than last year’s 6.8% increase from the previous year, the firm said. NRF derives its holiday forecast through modeling with economic indicators, including monthly retail sales, consumer spending, disposable personal income, employment, wages and inflation. The group's calculations exclude automobile dealers, gasoline stations and restaurants. The Labor Department’s snapshot of inflation released Wednesday showed that U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gas prices went back up again and many other goods and services became more expensive.

events.title: Trump says Fort Hood shooter's execution will not be livestreamed
events.summary: President Trump said in a Thursday Truth Social post that the execution of the convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan by firing squad will not be live-streamed. The big picture: The president's post walks back an idea that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pitched last week, setting off an avalanche of bipartisan condemnation. Driving the news: " He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," Trump's post read. He added, "That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose." Trump noted that he thinks "streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die." That seemingly included Vice President JD Vance , who said he wouldn't watch the execution. House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) warned footage of the execution could become a "recruiting tool for future terrorists." What they're saying: Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement provided to Axios that Trump and Secretary Hegseth discussed the decision ahead of the Truth Social post. Parnell added: "The Secretary supports the President's decision, and they are completely aligned." Catch up quick: The Pentagon previously confirmed that the December execution would be streamed after Hegseth said in an interview with Real America's Voice that it would be made "public." But the plan received swift pushback from Republicans and Democrats in Congress alike, as well as from clergy and survivors of the horrific 2009 attack. Even though most Americans support executing Hasan, a vast majority oppose livestreaming his death by firing squad, according to an ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll out Thursday. Representatives for TikTok and Newsmax told Axios their platforms wouldn't allow execution livestreams or clips, Axios' Sara Fischer reported. Friction point: The reversal also comes after Axios' Marc Caputo reported that the president himself was privately expressing doubts about the public execution after being deluged with a chorus of negative sentiment. He was initially full-throated in his approval of the idea — but it took roughly a week for the plan to crumble. Go deeper: Hegseth's public execution plan meets the age of viral violence Editor's note: This story has been updated with a statement from the Pentagon.

events.title: 'I paid thousands to a company for jobs that never came'
events.summary: Apurv Patel said he paid Synetal Solutions £3,600 and claimed he was verbally promised a guaranteed sponsored job A company has been accused of promising jobs in the healthcare sector which never materialised, leaving people thousands of pounds out of pocket. Registered in 2025, Synetal Solutions Ltd says it offers career-focused training programmes in the healthcare and IT sectors. But the BBC has spoken to a number of people who claim they were promised training and support to secure sponsored healthcare jobs that never became available to apply for. London Citizens Advice says it has seen an increase in recruitment-related scams since the government stopped overseas recruitment for care workers , external . The charity described the firm's practices as "unethical". Synetal Solutions says it "takes these concerns seriously and disputes the broad allegation that its services or candidate outcomes are fictitious". Apurv Patel, who has been in the UK on a Skilled Worker visa since 2023, said he paid Synetal Solutions £3,600 across February and March for healthcare training after he and a friend were verbally promised guaranteed sponsored jobs. Eight months later he has received no job offers, interviews or meaningful employment support, he said. "I'm frustrated. I paid money, I wasted my time. I did whatever they wanted without any result," he said. "It's had a miserable effect on my family and finances." Patel said he did receive some training but described it as poor quality and ultimately "worthless". Having previously worked for two years as a healthcare assistant, he said he became concerned when a trainer was unable to answer routine questions about care work. "She didn't give us any answers and we realised she didn't have any experience of healthcare," he said. The company disputes claims that training was ineffective. He also alleged communication with the company deteriorated after he made his second payment, with responses sometimes taking several days. Patel has since complained to his bank and sought help from Citizens Advice. The BBC has seen emails from the company advertising a "three-month recruitment programme" offering "training and placement with sponsorship" for £5,500. Home Office guidance , external states agencies may charge for services such as training or CV-writing assistance, but cannot charge fees solely for finding, or attempting to find, employment. Responding to questions about its marketing, Synetal Solutions said: "We acknowledge the 'guarantee' wording in the emails supplied and recognise that contractual terms alone do not resolve concerns about those assurances." As part of its programme, Synetal Solutions created accounts for trainees on iHasco, a health and social care training platform. The BBC contacted iHasco, which confirmed the company was a customer. However, it said its terms did not permit customers to resell its training content to individuals who were not employees. The company said it was reviewing Synetal Solutions' account and would take appropriate action if necessary. Synetal Solutions said it had acted in accordance with its agreement with iHasco. The Care Quality Commission said there was no single qualification that automatically qualified someone to work as a care worker. Instead, providers are responsible for ensuring employees are appropriately trained and competent for their roles. The BBC also contacted a number of healthcare organisations whose logos appeared on Synetal Solutions' website as examples of employers where graduates had worked. Those organisations that responded said they had no links to the company. Some also said they had not authorised the use of their branding, and some said they would not accept certificates provided through the company's training. Daniel Blake says the way Synetal Solutions has operated is unethical Daniel Blake, director of London Citizens Advice, described the company's approach as "exploitative". "The promises that were made are impossible promises," he said. "They are targeting people with vulnerable immigration status. "This company is asking for large sums of money upfront without any reputable standards, without any reputable evidence of success, and yet when it goes wrong they are refusing to take any responsibility. "For us, it seems a very unethical way of conducting business." He added that no reputable recruitment agency would guarantee a successful outcome without first assessing a candidate and matching them to a suitable role, and urged anybody asked to pay large sums upfront to seek independent advice. "If it seems too good to be true, it probably is," he said. The company's website stated: "Synetal Solutions provides the right support, guidance, and guaranteed job placement to help you succeed." But since the BBC contacted Synetal Solutions mentions of job guarantees were removed from the website.

events.title: Trump FDA nominee played key role in overhaul of childhood vaccine policy
events.summary: The News Heidi Overton, President Donald Trump’s nominee to run the Food and Drug Administration, played a larger role in driving the process to reduce the number of vaccines the government recommends to children than emerged during her Senate confirmation last month, when Republican senators asked her whether she’d stand up to anti-vaccine voices in the administration. An aide on the president’s Domestic Policy Council, Overton helped edit and craft a scientific justification that was used to underpin cutting the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommendations from 17 to 11 vaccines in January, according to a senior administration official and three people familiar with the process. “It was Heidi driving this whole thing,” said a former senior administration official, noting that Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. supported the policy push. The Senate health committee did not vote on whether to advance Overton to the Senate floor before departing earlier this month, leaving the decision for the lame duck session. If Republicans ultimately support her, Overton will lead the agency responsible for vaccine policy after making a bigger contribution to the Trump administration’s effort to reverse decades of American policy on childhood vaccines than was widely understood. “Every vaccine on the US market right now are safe and effective according to the FDA,” Overton told Senate Health Committee Chair Bill Cassidy, R-La, during the hearing. But throughout the fall of 2025, Overton built consensus across health agencies around narrowing the list of recommended universal childhood vaccines, meeting with Trump administration officials including Kennedy; then-FDA Commissioner Marty Makary; Mehmet Oz, who oversees Medicare and Medicaid; Jay Bhattacharya, the director of the National Institutes of Health; and Stefanie Spear, a senior HHS official and close confidant to Kennedy. Others in the administration say that Overton’s work is a reflection of the nature of a White House policy job, not her own priorities. “I think there is a misperception that because Heidi is the point of contact for the White House on a lot of issues, that she personally is doing something because of her personal views or or motivations,” a separate administration official said, noting the White House is “top-down.” The Atlantic reported in July that Overton had been part of a team that created an initial draft of childhood vaccine recommendations. Kennedy was prepared to endorse Denmark’s vaccine schedule, which recommends vaccinations against 10 diseases for all children, as an option for American parents based on the memo. But Kennedy’s December press conference was canceled at the last minute, according to three people familiar with the discussions. Before the scheduled event, HHS lawyers raised concerns to senior health officials that it lacked evidence and would be susceptible to legal challenges, two of the people said. On Jan. 5, former Health Deputy Secretary and then-acting CDC Director Jim O’Neill signed a decision memo that adopted a revised childhood immunization schedule based on the assessment conducted by Høeg, the acting director of the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research at the time, and Martin Kulldorff, an HHS aide. The American Academy of Pediatrics challenged the revised schedule in court , and a federal judge put it on hold in March. Know More When Trump nominated Overton in August to lead the FDA, prominent Make America Healthy Again activists objected, saying she would be too friendly toward drugmakers if confirmed. “This narrative took hold that Heidi was not aligned with Kennedy on this, was more aligned with pharma [on] vaccine stuff, and was in favor of a more maximal vaccine schedule,” the former senior administration official said. “And that’s just not the case, not what happened.” An HHS official said Overton was tasked with putting Trump’s policy priority into a document that was “suitable for distribution throughout the White House.” “Someone needed to sort of pull the different strands together and make sure they came together into a quilt that was at least representative of what the different folks were trying to do,” the HHS official said. “The president had already expressed, and has continued to express a very strong desire to revisit vaccines, in part because he’s concerned about complications. This is not something that she would have personally desired. I am quite confident.” At her Senate confirmation hearing in September, Cassidy pressed Overton on her commitment to defending the safety and efficacy of vaccines, and asked whether she’d stand up to Trump under pressure. “If he asks you to do something which goes against the guarantee you’ve made to the American people through us, what will you do?” Cassidy asked. “I would give him my best advice,” Overton replied. Cassidy is a trained gastroenterologist and liver specialist who is leaving office this year after losing a primary election where Trump endorsed his challenger and has said Kennedy’s vaccine approach broke commitments made during his own confirmation process. His office declined to comment when asked about Overton’s involvement in drafting the scientific justification document. When Trump nominated Overton, Cassidy posted that her involvement in Trump’s “nonsensical vaccine executive order” in August , which aimed to break up the established measles, mumps and rubella vaccine into multiple doses, was “almost disqualifying.” Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester, D-Del., pressed Overton at the confirmation hearing about whether she thought splitting the MMR vaccine into multiple shots or reducing the number of childhood vaccines were “good options.” “My job in my current role is to take the president’s directive, provide options to him for him to make the decision,” Overton responded. Notable Overton was quiet on her own opinions during her confirmation hearing , STAT reported . If Democrats take control of the Senate next year, they’ll confirm “very few” of Trump’s nominees , Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer told Semafor’s Burgess Everett .

events.title: Perplexity to give away its AI security software
events.summary: The Scoop Perplexity is giving away the software it has been using to combat rogue AI agents, the company told Semafor Thursday. Its “AI sandbox,” which it calls SPACE, is now an open source project, allowing outside developers to use the tool, which it says can keep AI agents contained. Perplexity said it’s lined up partners, including CoreWeave, Akamai and Crusoe, which have agreed to offer SPACE to customers. Sandboxes, or isolated environments for testing and running AI models, have become a hot topic in the tech industry in the wake of reports from AI labs of models escaping their constraints, finding their way onto the open web and hacking unsuspecting victims like Hugging Face and the Australian government. While AI companies focus on “alignment,” or training models to behave themselves, the security industry has been increasingly advocating erecting strict guardrails around AI models. “A lot of companies are thinking about how to build secure AI agents, and in many cases they hit a wall,” said Zibi Braniecki, a member of the technical staff at Perplexity, in an interview with Semafor. “We have a solution.” Perplexity said it tested SPACE by giving nine frontier models instructions to try to break out. In 118 tries, none of them did, while Perplexity found they were able to break out of other sandboxes that were not open sourced. Know More Braniecki likened the effort to make SPACE open source to what happened with web browsers as the internet developed — companies came together to build guardrails that allowed secure browsing and online commerce. “Right now, we’re thinking too small,” he said. Other companies like Nvidia have also released open-source security tools, such as Nvidia OpenShell, which runs AI agents in a sandbox and limits what they can reach. Perplexity said SPACE also helps reduce wasted compute, which can be a byproduct of strict sandboxing.

events.title: "Mommy and daddy" play nice: Apple and Meta team up to bring open-source Muse to Macs
events.summary: Apple and Meta, whose leaders have spent years trading barbs over privacy and the future of computing, are joining forces to bring one of America's most powerful open-weight AI models to Apple's high-end Macs. Why it matters: The collaboration marks a striking détente between two longtime Silicon Valley rivals, underscoring how the AI race is reshaping relationships across the technology industry. The companies still compete over devices and the next generation of computing, but both see an opportunity in bringing powerful AI capabilities to personal computers. "We're excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again," Meta's AI chief Alexandr Wang told Axios. Driving the news: Meta is releasing Muse Spark Open, a model similar to Muse Spark 1.3, that it says is the most powerful U.S.-developed open-weight AI model available. Meta joins a host of Western AI companies that have released powerful open-weight systems that promise to slash AI costs, provide companies with more control and offer an alternative to the Chinese AI ecosystem. Nvidia on Tuesday released updated versions of its Nemotron family of models, and U.S.-based Reflection AI and France's Mistral both released new open source models last week. As proof of Muse Spark Open's capabilities, Meta worked with Apple to make the model run locally across two or four connected Mac Studios powered by Apple's M5 Ultra chips, using Apple's MLX framework. Zoom in : The prospect of a powerful model — it has 816 billion parameters — running on Apple hardware offers a proof of concept about just how much companies will be able to build their own AI systems. That could give companies more alternatives to Nvidia GPUs and proprietary models from leading AI labs, potentially shifting some of the economics of AI. Meta's model will be free to download, with a license allowing commercial use, and will also be available through cloud providers and developer tools. What they're saying: Wang said the companies have been working together for several months, with Daniel Gross, a former Apple executive now at Meta, playing a key role in bringing the two sides together. "I think he played a really big role in kind of getting the two companies to work nicely together," Wang said in a telephone interview. Flashback: Apple executive chairman Tim Cook and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg have repeatedly clashed over privacy and their competing business models. In 2018, amid Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal, Cook was asked what he would do if he were Zuckerberg. "I wouldn't be in this situation," Cook replied. Zuckerberg called Cook's comments "extremely glib." The rivalry intensified in 2021, when Apple introduced new privacy protections that struck at the heart of Facebook's ad business. Zuckerberg reportedly told employees that Facebook needed to "inflict pain" on Apple over the dispute, according to the Wall Street Journal. The big picture: The AI race is making for some strange bedfellows, scrambling longstanding Silicon Valley rivalries and even bringing together political adversaries. Anthropic is leasing up to $15 billion per year of computing capacity from Elon Musk's SpaceX, even as it competes with his AI company. Microsoft, OpenAI's longtime partner, is investing billions in rival Anthropic and incorporating its Claude models into its own products. And in Washington, progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders and MAGA strategist Steve Bannon have found common ground in calling for tougher AI safeguards and challenging the power of Big Tech. Between the lines: The Apple-Meta collaboration doesn't mean the companies have resolved their differences, but it suggests those disagreements no longer prevent them from working together when their interests align. Meta benefits from making its AI models widely available, while Apple can showcase the capabilities of its most powerful computers. And because the model runs locally, Meta doesn't receive users' prompts or other information — sidestepping the privacy concerns that have long divided the companies. "Meta has no control or visibility to any of that," Wang said of how developers use the model. Yes, but: Making powerful AI models openly available raises concerns that bad actors could remove safeguards and use the technology for cyberattacks or biological threats. What we're watching: Whether the collaboration marks the beginning of a broader relationship between Apple and Meta. For now, Apple is helping demonstrate that Meta's AI models can run locally on its computers. A more significant step would be Apple incorporating Meta's models into Apple Intelligence, giving the Facebook parent a role in powering Apple's own AI features. The bottom line: Wang acknowledged that Apple and Meta will continue to compete in some areas, but said that doesn't have to prevent them from working together. "Where it makes sense to collaborate and partner, we want to be able to do so," he said.

events.title: Adobe and NVIDIA Expand Collaboration to Speed Agentic Creation
events.summary: News Summary: Adobe is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to optimize its flagship tools including Adobe Photoshop, Premiere, Substance 3D, Frame.io and Brand Concierge, delivering faster AI-powered creation, production and personalization. Adobe is bringing the power of the NVIDIA RTX Spark superchip to its agentic creative applications Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D. Optimized to take full advantage of RTX Spark, these applications deliver up to 2x faster AI processing, editing, color and effects, helping creatives iterate faster and stay in their creative flow. Adobe Brand Concierge is now optimized with NVIDIA Nemotron open models, providing enterprises a flexible and efficient way to deliver high-quality conversational experiences at scale, with NVIDIA also selecting Brand Concierge to power relevant and contextual customer interactions on NVIDIA.com. Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE), the global technology leader that unleashes creativity, productivity and customer experiences through innovative tools and platforms, and NVIDIA today announced an expansion of their partnership to optimize Adobe’s flagship tools including Adobe Photoshop, Premiere, Substance 3D, Frame.io and Brand Concierge, delivering faster AI-powered creation, production and personalization. This work builds on Adobe and NVIDIA’s strategic partnership announced in March, which brings together Adobe’s creative and marketing workflows, models and technology with NVIDIA’s open models, libraries, research and accelerated computing to accelerate creative, production and marketing workflows across video, images, 3D and other creative media. That collaboration includes GPU acceleration for media ingestion and intelligence in Frame.io, as well as ongoing work around Adobe Substance 3D, Adobe Firefly Foundry and 3D digital twin workflows for enterprise customers. “Creative workflows are more multimodal than ever, with many projects spanning images, video, audio, motion and 3D, making performance critical to helping creatives stay focused on their ideas and craft,” said Deepa Subramaniam, vice president, product marketing, creative professionals, Adobe. “By partnering with NVIDIA to optimize Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D for RTX Spark and accelerating Frame.io in the cloud, we’re delivering the performance creatives need to bring their ideas to life.” “AI agents are helping creators unlock deeper and richer workflows using the Adobe applications they know and love,” said Jason Paul, vice president, local AI, NVIDIA. “Powered by RTX Spark, Adobe’s optimized tools deliver up to 2x faster performance to accelerate these new workflows.”   Empowering Creatives With Faster Adobe Tools Rearchitected With NVIDIA Creative professionals today move between image, video, motion and 3D, sometimes all within the same project. As AI increasingly becomes part of the creative process, they need technology that keeps pace with the speed of their ideas and the complexity of their workflows. As an industry leader in creativity, Adobe’s tools apply decades of creative expertise to amplify human potential and make it easier to quickly turn ideas into impactful work. Adobe is bringing the power of the NVIDIA RTX Spark superchip, launching tomorrow, Oct. 16, to its agentic creative applications Photoshop , Premiere and Substance 3D . RTX-accelerated and optimized to take full advantage of RTX Spark’s unified memory and AI compute, these applications deliver up to 2x faster AI processing, editing, color and effects, helping creatives iterate faster and stay in their creative flow. Adobe rearchitected Photoshop around GPU-accelerated compositing to be faster and more responsive for creative tasks from removing distractions with the Remove Tool to applying effects like Gaussian Blur and Light Leaks directly on canvas. Some of the most demanding post-production workflows in Premiere, from playback and rendering to effects, color and AI-powered tools, are RTX-accelerated and optimized for RTX Spark. This results in real, tangible speed gains for popular audio and video features in Premiere like Enhance Speech and Object Mask. For 3D artists using Substance 3D Painter, RTX Spark speeds up the heaviest steps around texturing. Accelerating Cloud Video Workflows With Frame.io and NVIDIA Adobe is also using NVIDIA accelerated computing to speed cloud media processing and intelligent content discovery for Adobe Frame.io , helping production teams find and use growing media libraries faster. The updated Frame.io pipeline uses NVIDIA video acceleration, including NVIDIA NVDEC for hardware-accelerated decoding and NVIDIA TensorRT ™ with CUDA ®   for content preprocessing and embedding generation. Moving compute-intensive video decoding, preprocessing and embedding generation onto NVIDIA GPUs lets Frame.io process media faster and make it searchable sooner, while supporting more responsive discovery across large content libraries.   Early performance results from selected Frame.io transcode and search workloads show: Approximately 5x faster embedding generation 4-5x improvement in P95 processing latency An approximately 80% smaller search proxy For creative teams, these gains mean uploaded content becomes searchable sooner, larger libraries refresh more efficiently, and discovery and review stay frictionless as media volumes grow. Personalized Conversational Experiences With Adobe Brand Concierge Optimized on NVIDIA Nemotron Brands also want more choice and value from the AI models powering personalized experiences. Open models can help meet that need, providing a flexible and efficient way to deliver high-quality, responsive conversations at enterprise scale. Adobe and NVIDIA worked together to optimize Brand Concierge using NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models. This version will be available to enterprise customers later this year. NVIDIA has also selected Brand Concierge to drive personalized conversational experiences grounded in organizational data and content. This enables NVIDIA to tailor interactions on their website based on customer needs, while leveraging Nemotron to deliver fast, high-quality responses at scale. Sparking Creativity, to the MAX Get ready for what’s next — with three days of creative skill-building, visionary keynotes and valuable connections at Adobe MAX , running Nov. 10-12. Adobe and NVIDIA will showcase the latest advancements for creators alongside their hardware partners. ]]>

events.title: Windows 11 gets faster, more connected and easier to use
events.summary: What’s new in Windows 11: Everyday experiences, reimagined Every day, your PC helps you get things done, stay connected, capture ideas and make time for what you enjoy. That’s why Windows 11 continues to evolve, starting with a faster, more dependable and refined experience. Throughout the year, we’ve worked with the Windows Insider community on improvements to Windows that are now beginning to roll out broadly, with more to come. That same care shapes our latest Windows experiences, building on these foundational improvements with new possibilities that make everyday moments on your PC simpler and more intuitive. From new features for gamers, to a modernized Photos experience, to more seamless phone to PC integration, Windows is built to support the way you work, create, play and connect. A faster, more responsive Windows experience Responsiveness shapes nearly every experience on your PC. It’s the difference between staying in your flow and waiting for your device to catch up. That’s why we’ve continued to invest across Windows , from the platform and shell to the apps people use every day, to make Windows feel faster, more responsive and more efficient. The result is a Windows experience that’s up to 20% more responsive , with improvements you can feel as soon as you boot into your PC and extending to Start, File Explorer, Search, Snipping Tool, Microsoft 365, Edge and more 1 . A big part of that work is making smarter use of memory and system resources. We’ve improved memory management and efficiency across Windows to help keep more of your PC’s resources focused on what you’re actively doing. That work can make an especially meaningful difference on PCs with 8GB of memory. Windows can now keep up to 2GB more of your active data in memory instead of moving it to slower storage, helping your PC stay responsive as you open more apps or browser tabs. Windows is also making additional memory-saving improvements that reduce background memory use. For example, on PCs with 8GB of memory or less, Widgets load only when you open them, making more than 200 MB of memory available for your apps and other work 2 . It’s one example of the broader work underway to reduce the Windows memory footprint and deliver a fast, responsive experience across the PCs people use every day, an area we’ve made an explicit focus for Windows. But a great Windows experience isn’t only about speed. It’s also about making your PC feel dependable, less disruptive and more your own. We’re giving you more flexibility to personalize Start and your taskbar , including choosing where it appears on your screen, while making Widgets cleaner and quieter so you have more control over what gets your attention. And we’ve improved Windows Update to give you greater control over when updates happen and better coordinate updates to reduce restarts, while continuing to reduce the time it takes to apply an update. We’re also improving the everyday interactions you depend on. Bluetooth headphones work more reliably on Windows, with smoother pairing, reconnection, audio and calls, including an AirPods pairing experience that’s up to 15 seconds faster 3 . And we’ve made signing in with Windows Hello easier, faster and more reliable, with improvements to both face and fingerprint recognition. Alongside that work, we’re partnering with our hardware ecosystem through the Driver Quality Initiative to improve driver stability, reliability, security and performance across Windows devices. The result is a Windows experience that feels faster, more responsive and more thoughtfully designed around you, whether you’re opening an app, finding a file, connecting your headphones, arranging your taskbar the way you want or simply getting back to what you were doing. For hundreds of millions of people each day, Windows search on the taskbar is where intent begins. It’s one of the quickest ways to get started, whether finding a file, opening an app, or changing a setting. This release builds on the search quality improvements we delivered in recent months, with clearer results and more control over suggestions. Now, we are carrying those improvements forward with a new interface and expanding search from a place for finding information into a place for getting things done. Finding the right result is often only the first step. After finding what you’re looking for, you often need to navigate to another destination to complete the task. Actions allow you to complete common Windows tasks directly from the search results. When searching for a system setting like dark mode or night light, you can now make the relevant change without opening Settings or searching for the right sub-menu. Search can also help with managing your workspace, like minimizing or arranging open windows, and coming soon, the ability to interact with your connected phone. These actions are designed to make common tasks faster and more intuitive: simply search and act directly from the taskbar. The new Windows Search experience is available to Windows Insiders today and will roll out more broadly later this year. Learn more about the new Windows Search experience . Move between your phone and PC seamlessly When you’re in the middle of something on your PC, your phone’s messages, apps and files should be within reach too. Windows 11 brings more of your phone experience to your desktop, so you can reply to a message, answer phone calls, open apps, and keep going without reaching for another device 4 . Preview messages and notifications from your Android phone or iPhone in Start to see what needs your attention. When a conversation needs a reply, open it in a window focused on your chat, send your response and get back to what you were doing. Quick Settings keeps useful phone controls close, whether you want to silence or ring a misplaced phone. With a supported Android phone, open your phone apps in separate, resizable windows on your desktop, with room to work on the larger screen alongside your other apps. Browse your phone files in File Explorer and open what you need without switching devices. And when you take a photo on your phone, a notification on your PC lets you open it with one click, ready for a closer look. When you do move between devices, Resume helps you pick up supported activities where you left off instead of finding your place again. It’s your phone and PC working together, so you can stay connected from the screen you’re already using. Spend less time searching for your photos and more time enjoying them. The new Microsoft Photos app brings images from your PC and connected libraries into one fast, beautiful Gallery, with more of your collection in view. Whether you’re revisiting a favorite trip or browsing everyday snapshots, it’s easier to see what you have and rediscover moments worth keeping close. Find a favorite by describing it in your own words or bring memories together in albums to share.
